alerts.title: Carbamazepine reduces DTG levels
alerts.message: Guidelines state carbamazepine decreases dolutegravir (DTG) levels by 30-70%. The patient started carbamazepine two weeks ago and now has a detectable viral load of 1,240 copies/mL despite reported good adherence. This timing suggests the drug interaction is a likely cause of virologic failure. The guideline recommends using valproic acid as an alternative anti-epileptic.

evidence.recommended_action: Consider switching anti-epileptic therapy to valproic acid as per guidelines to avoid DTG level reduction.

alerts.title: Carbamazepine toxicity present
alerts.message: The patient has symptoms (dizziness, unsteady gait, tremor, nystagmus) and a supratherapeutic carbamazepine level of 14 mcg/mL (therapeutic range 4-12). The clinician's plan to reduce the dose and repeat the level is appropriate. However, the concurrent hyponatremia (Na 128 mmol/L) is a known side effect of carbamazepine and may contribute to neurological symptoms.

evidence.recommended_action: Implement the planned carbamazepine dose reduction, monitor sodium, and assess for resolution of neurological symptoms.

alerts.title: Viral load >1000 copies/mL
alerts.message: Guidelines state a viral load >1000 copies/mL at repeat testing, following intensified adherence counseling, is a criterion for considering third-line ART eligibility. The patient's viral load is 1,240 copies/mL. Adherence counseling and a repeat test are required before considering regimen change.

evidence.recommended_action: Provide intensified adherence counseling and schedule a repeat viral load test as per protocol.

alerts.title: Elevated ALT
alerts.message: Patient's ALT is elevated at 68 U/L. Guidelines note that drug-related side effects, including liver toxicity, can occur early after starting a new medication. Both carbamazepine and sodium valproate are known hepatotoxic drugs. Non-drug causes such as concurrent infection should also be considered.

evidence.recommended_action: Monitor ALT trend, review all hepatotoxic medications, and investigate other potential causes of liver injury.
